stem.text: The concentration of a medicine in a patient's blood is modeled by \( C(t) = 95 - 55 e^{- \frac{t}{6}} \) milligrams per liter, for \( 0 \le t \le 18 \), where t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find \( C'(6) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( C'(6) = 3.372 \), so at time t = 6 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 3.372 milligrams per liter per hour.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the model to get the rate, \( C'(t) = \frac{55 e^{- \frac{t}{6}}}{6} \).
With a calculator, \( C'(6) = 3.372 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 6 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 3.372 milligrams per liter per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change
